findings.title: Wire the streaming fast path into the actual OBJ progress load before closing this queue
findings.evidence: The new direct destination requires expected.bytes. The sole real onProgress call is source-worker OBJ download, whose expected object contains only sha256. All bytes-bearing MTL/nativeLoad calls omit onProgress. Actual source-worker execution with its production branch logic recorded OBJ progress=true, expected.bytes absent, directPreallocationEligible=false; MTL progress=false, expected.bytes=3, eligible=false. Thus nonconstrained cold OBJ loading retains chunks plus joined output, exactly the peak targeted by the queue. Existing new unit tests synthesize bytes+progress and never execute the caller wiring.
findings.impact: Optimization is dead for real game downloads; queue/report claim of reduced production buffering is not established. Integrity checks and stream cleanup remain sound.
findings.suggested_action: Use an authenticated actual media-OBJ byte size in the progress call, or a safe different streaming approach, with an integration test exercising source-worker. Do not pass source-tree f.size blindly: Vss_Yunohana.obj inventory size133 describes the Git LFS pointer, not the media OBJ. Alternatively retain/reject this queue as unimplemented with a concrete reason.

closure.result: Closed: production nonconstrained worker now passes authenticated actual LFS payload bytes together with the progress callback. Constrained worker retains prior no-size/no-progress contract; unknown/new SHA retains fallback.
closure.independent_evidence: Read-only inspected the actual worker wiring and real SHA-keyed sourceObjectBytes lookup. Independently validated all23 bundled inventories against pinned SHA256, reconstructed canonical LFS pointers using stage payload oid plus proposed byte size, and matched Git blob SHA1 plus pointer size. Exactly18 payloads satisfy existing64MiB upfront bound;5 oversized payloads retain checked chunk fallback. Unknown SHA returns undefined. No HTTP Content-Length enters allocation authority. Source SHA256/byte verification still precedes cache publication.
